Why do lymph nodes swell when you're sick?

The small lymph nodes in your neck or armpit swell because they're busy making defenders to fight off the germs.
copy.tl:

Namamaga ang maliliit na kulani sa leeg o kilikili dahil masiglang gumagawa ito ng panlaban sa mga germ.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga manghupong ang lymph node kon magsakit?

Manghupong ang gagmay nga lymph node sa liog o ilok tungod busy sila sa paghimo og panalipod batok sa germ.

Who made the very first compass?

The ancient Chinese made the first compass using lodestone to find direction!

Sino ang gumawa ng pinakaunang compass?

Ang mga sinaunang Tsino ang gumawa ng unang compass gamit ang lodestone para malaman ang direksyon.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang naghimo sa pinakaunang compass?

Ang karaang mga Intsik ang naghimo sa unang compass gamit ang lodestone aron mahibal-an ang direksyon.

copy.tl: Biglang hindi na kumakapit ang gawa mong electromagnet? Malamang ubos na ang baterya! Walang kuryente, walang magnet. Palitan mo lang ang baterya, at babalik ang lakas nito!
copy.bis: Kalit nga dili na mokupot ang imong gihimo nga electromagnet? Lagmit nahurot na ang baterya! Walay kuryente, walay magnet. Ilisi lang ang baterya, ug mobalik ang kusog niini!

copy.tl: Ang magnet na hugis-U, parang sapatos ng kabayo, ay tinatawag na horseshoe magnet. Ang galing, 'di ba?
copy.bis: Ang magnet nga porma ug letra U, sama sa sapatos sa kabayo, gitawag nga horseshoe magnet. Nindot, 'di ba?

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They use a small magnet! It grips a metal plate to keep the door held tightly closed.

How do some cabinet doors stay perfectly shut?

They use a small magnet! It grips a metal plate to keep the door held tightly closed.

Paano nananatiling sarado ang ilang pinto ng kabinet?

Gumagamit ito ng maliit na magnet! Nakakapit ito sa metal na plato para sarado ang pinto.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpabilin nga sirado ang pultahan sa ubang kabinet?

Naggamit kini og gamay nga magnet! Mokapyot kini sa metal nga plato para magpabilin kining sirado.

copy.tl: Ang magnetic field ng Daigdig ay humuhuli ng maliliit na partikulo mula sa Araw! Nagtitipon sila sa mga rehiyong parang sinturon na nakapalibot sa planeta. Tinatawag itong radiation belts.
copy.bis: Ang magnetic field sa Kalibutan modakop sa gagmay nga mga partikulo gikan sa Adlaw! Nagtigom sila sa mga rehiyon nga sama sa bakus nga naglibot sa planeta. Gitawag kini nga radiation belts.

copy.en: Extreme heat can weaken or destroy a magnet! The tiny parts inside that line up neatly get all jumbled up. Once jumbled, they no longer point together, so the magnetism fades away.
copy.tl: Ang sobrang init ay pwedeng magpahina o sirain ang isang magnet! Ang maliliit na bahagi sa loob na nakaayos nang maayos ay nagugulo. Kapag nagulo na, hindi na sila sabay-sabay, kaya nawawala ang magnetismo.
copy.bis: Ang grabe ka init mahimong magpahuyang o maguba sa usa ka magnet! Ang gagmay nga bahin sa sulod nga han-ay magubot. Kung magubot na, dili na sila magdungan, mao nga mawala ang pagka-magnet.

copy.bis: Sayon makita ang makahiya sa Pilipinas kay motubo kini nga mag-inusara sa daplin sa dalan ug sa mga nataran.

copy.en:
Where does the water go when a makahiya leaf folds?

It isn't lost — it just moves into neighboring cells. When one side loses water and goes limp, the leaf bends and closes toward that side.
copy.tl:
Saan napupunta ang tubig kapag tumiklop ang dahon ng makahiya?

Hindi ito nawawala — lumilipat lang ito sa kabilang mga selula. Kapag nawalan ng tubig ang isang panig at lumambot, doon napupunta at nagsasara ang dahon.
copy.bis:
Asa muadto ang tubig kon mutiklop ang dahon sa makahiya?

Dili kini mawala — mubalhin lang kini sa silingang mga selula. Kon mawad-an og tubig ang usa ka kilid ug muhumok, didto mutakilid ug musira ang dahon.

No! The male mosquito never bites -- it only drinks nectar or plant juice to survive.

Hindi! Hindi kumakagat ang lalaking lamok -- umiinom lang ito ng nektar o katas ng halaman para mabuhay.

Dili! Dili mopaak ang laki nga lamok -- moinom ra kini og nektar o duga sa tanom aron mabuhi.

What's unusual about the mandarin fish?

The mandarin fish is one of few animals with real blue-green skin color, and instead of scales, it makes toxic mucus to protect itself.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kakaiba sa mandarin fish?

Ang mandarin fish ay isa sa iilang hayop na may tunay na berde-asul na kulay sa balat, at sa halip na kaliskis, gumagawa ito ng makalasong uhog para sa proteksyon.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang lahi sa mandarin fish?

Ang mandarin fish usa sa pipila ka hayop nga adunay tinuod nga asul-berde nga kolor sa panit, ug imbes nga kaliskis, naghimo kini og makahilo nga uhog aron sa proteksyon.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Time from flower to ripe fruit is phenology, not pollination, seed production, or propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it takes a few months for a mango fruit to grow and ripen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: Ripening time is one plant stage, not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

copy.en: After flowering, it takes a few months for a mango fruit to grow and ripen.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos mamulaklak, umaabot ng ilang buwan bago lumaki at humihinog ang bunga ng mangga.
copy.bis: Human mamulak, mokabat og pipila ka bulan ayha modako ug mahinog ang bunga sa mangga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mangoes are nutritious and rich in vitamin C, which is good for the body!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a nutritional fact about mangoes but does not teach students to identify basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only mentions food indirectly as a nutrient source, without addressing the concept of needs.

copy.en: Mangoes are nutritious and rich in vitamin C, which is good for the body!
copy.tl: Ang mangga ay masustansya at mayaman sa bitamina C na nakakabuti sa katawan!
copy.bis: Ang mangga masustansya ug daghan og bitamina C nga maayo sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a regular crab that recently molted
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that a soft-shell crab is a molted crab, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Molting is only implicitly tied to growth; the card does not teach that living things grow, respond, or reproduce.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a regular crab that recently molted
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions molting, which is part of a crab's life cycle, but it does not use a flow chart or compare life-cycle stages of animals. The format-required competency explicitly requires a flow chart comparing stages, which is absent.

copy.en:
Is a soft-shell crab a different crab?

No! A 'soft-shell crab' is just a regular crab that recently molted — once its shell hardens again, it's an ordinary hard crab.
copy.tl:
Ibang uri ba ng alimango ang soft-shell crab?

Hindi! Ang 'soft-shell crab' ay ordinaryong alimango lamang na katatapos mag-molt — kapag tumigas na ang balat, magiging karaniwang matigas na alimango ulit ito.
copy.bis:
Lahi ba nga alimango ang soft-shell crab?

Dili! Ang 'soft-shell crab' usa lang ka ordinaryong alimango nga bag-o pa lang nakabalhin og balat — kon mogahi na ang balat, mahimo na usab kining ordinaryong gahi nga alimango.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the land is also sinking, so the sea seems to rise even faster!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions land subsidence in Manila making sea level rise appear faster. This touches on a local impact of climate change (sea level rise), but it does not identify the impact as a consequence of global climate change, nor does it suggest any individual actions to reduce global warming. The competency requires both identifying local impacts and suggesting mitigation actions; the card provides only a vague statement about sinking land, which is more about subsidence than climate change itself. Thus it is related but not direct instructional support.

copy.en: In places like Manila, the land is also sinking, so the sea seems to rise even faster!
copy.tl: Sa ilang lugar gaya ng Maynila, lumulubog din ang lupa, kaya parang mas mabilis tumaas ang dagat!
copy.bis: Sa pipila ka lugar sama sa Manila, naglubog usab ang yuta, busa morag mas paspas mosaka ang dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because its folded front legs look just like a person praying with hands together!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the front legs of a praying mantis but only explains the name origin based on their appearance. It does not describe the role of legs for movement or gathering food, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

copy.en:
Why is it called a praying mantis?

Because its folded front legs look just like a person praying with hands together!
copy.tl:
Bakit tinawag itong praying mantis?

Dahil ang nakatiklop nitong mga paa ay parang taong nagdarasal!
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag kining praying mantis?

Tungod kay ang gilukot niini nga mga paa morag tawo nga nag-ampo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The mantis shrimp's eyes sit on stalks and can each swivel separately, looking two ways at once!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (eyes on stalks) but does not identify a role in moving or gathering food, which is the focus of the competency. Eyes are not among the examples (head, legs, wings) and their function here is vision, not locomotion or feeding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The mantis shrimp's eyes sit on stalks and can each swivel separately, looking two ways at once!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an eye structure but does not explain how it is an adaptation to better suit the environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or any environmental pressure. It is merely an interesting feature, not an example of evolutionary adaptation as required.

copy.en: The mantis shrimp's eyes sit on stalks and can each swivel separately, looking two ways at once!
copy.tl: Ang mga mata ng mantis shrimp ay nasa tangkay at kaya nilang gumalaw nang hiwalay sa magkaibang direksyon!
copy.bis: Ang mga mata sa mantis shrimp anaa sa tangkay ug makahimo molihok nga managlahi ang direksyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are "smashers" that punch with club-like limbs, and "spearers" that stab with sharp, pointed limbs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes outer body parts (club-like and pointed limbs) and their immediate function (punching/stabbing), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. The card does not address movement or food gathering; it focuses on weaponry/attack, which is not the stated role. Thus it is only related to the topic of animal body parts, not direct support for this competency.

copy.en:
What are the two kinds of mantis shrimp?

There are "smashers" that punch with club-like limbs, and "spearers" that stab with sharp, pointed limbs!
copy.tl:
Ano ang dalawang uri ng mantis shrimp?

May "smasher" na may martilyong pamuntok, at "spearer" na may matulis na pamana para manaksak!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang duha ka klase sa mantis shrimp?

Adunay "smasher" nga manuntok ug martilyo nga bukton, ug "spearer" nga manaksak ug talinis nga bukton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Marang spoils fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spoiling, which is a form of decomposition, but it does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting, or being degradable/biodegradable. It only gives a practical tip to eat it fresh, with no instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Marang spoils fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that marang spoils fast, which is a change in material, but it does not explain how changes in materials can be harmful to living or non-living things, nor does it reference trash disposal or burning household materials. The harm aspect is absent.

copy.en: Marang spoils fast, so it's best to eat it while it's still fresh off the tree.
copy.tl: Ang marang ay mabilis masira, kaya pinakamasarap itong kainin habang bago at sariwa pa.
copy.bis: Ang marang dali ra madaot, mao nga mas maayo kining kan-on samtang lab-as pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The March equinox happens around March 20 or 21 each year.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain, using models, how the tilt of the Earth affects the changes in the length of daytime at different times of the year
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the calendar date of the March equinox. It does not use models, discuss Earth's tilt, or explain changes in the length of daytime at different times of the year. The equinox date is only loosely related to the competency's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The March equinox happens around March 20 or 21 each year.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single equinox date and does not involve a Sun-Earth-Moon system model, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses. It does not demonstrate or explain any predictable pattern or event required by the competency.

copy.en:
When does the March equinox happen every year?

Look at the calendar! The March equinox happens around March 20 or 21 each year.
copy.tl:
Kailan nangyayari ang March equinox bawat taon?

Tingnan ang kalendaryo! Ang March equinox ay nangyayari tuwing mga Marso 20 o 21 bawat taon.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mahitabo ang March equinox matag tuig?

Tan-awa ang kalendaryo! Ang March equinox mahitabo sa mga Marso 20 o 21 matag tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Marie Curie! She won in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Marie Curie as a famous foreign scientist, but it does not mention any invention or discovery of hers. The competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s; the card only covers the scientist part, not the invention, so it does not directly support the full skill.

copy.en:
Who is the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences?

Marie Curie! She won in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).
copy.tl:
Sino ang tanging tao na nanalo ng Nobel Prize sa dalawang agham?

Si Marie Curie! Nanalo siya sa Physics (1903) at Chemistry (1911).
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang bugtong tawo nga nakadaog og Nobel Prize sa duha ka siyensiya?

Si Marie Curie! Nakadaog siya sa Physics (1903) ug Chemistry (1911).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: poison glands on its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a defensive feature (poison glands) of the cane toad but does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it provide an example of adaptation like mimicry or camouflage. It is only tangentially related to animal adaptations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: big rough-skinned toad
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the toad's rough skin and poison glands but does not identify outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. It does not support the competency's focus on body parts and their functions.

copy.en: The cane toad, or kamprag, is a big rough-skinned toad with poison glands on its body—never handle or eat it!
copy.tl: Ang kamprag o marine toad ay malaking palaka na magaspang ang balat at may lason sa mga glandula nito—huwag itong hawakan o kainin!
copy.bis: Ang kamprag o marine toad usa ka dako nga baki nga gaspang ang panit ug adunay hilo sa mga glandula niini—ayaw gyud kupti o kan-a!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mars is much colder than Earth, with temperatures often dropping well below zero degrees Celsius!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Mars' temperature, which is a main feature of one celestial object. However, the competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system, identifying names, main features, and general composition. A lone temperature fact does not directly support describing the solar system's structure or composition; it is only tangentially related to the broader topic.

copy.en: Mars is much colder than Earth, with temperatures often dropping well below zero degrees Celsius!
copy.tl: Mas malamig ang Mars kaysa Mundo, dahil ang temperatura nito ay madalas na nasa ilalim ng zero degrees Celsius!
copy.bis: Mas bugnaw ang Mars kaysa Yuta, kay ang temperatura niini kasagaran ubos pa sa zero degrees Celsius!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The moons Europa and Enceladus are thought to hide oceans of water under their ice.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card names two moons and notes they may have subsurface oceans, but it does not describe the general structure of the solar system, the major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition as required by the competency.

copy.en: Mars isn't the only place searched for life! The moons Europa and Enceladus are thought to hide oceans of water under their ice.
copy.tl: Hindi lang Mars ang hinahanapan ng buhay! Ang mga buwan na Europa at Enceladus ay pinaniniwalaang may karagatan ng tubig sa ilalim ng yelo.
copy.bis: Dili lang ang Mars ang ginapangitaan og kinabuhi! Ang mga bulan nga Europa ug Enceladus gituohan nga adunay kadagatan sa tubig ilalom sa ilang yelo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mars has two (2) moons! Their names are Phobos and Deimos.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about Mars's moons, but the competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system and identifying the names, main features, and general composition of major celestial objects. The card does not describe the solar system's structure or provide general features/composition of Mars or other celestial objects; it only names two moons of one planet.

copy.en:
How many moons does Mars have?

Mars has two (2) moons! Their names are Phobos and Deimos.
copy.tl:
Ilang buwan ang meron sa Mars?

Ang Mars ay may dalawang (2) buwan! Ang mga pangalan nila ay Phobos at Deimos.
copy.bis:
Pila ka bulan ang Mars?

Ang Mars adunay duha (2) ka bulan! Ang ilang mga ngalan mao ang Phobos ug Deimos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Mars, a major celestial object, and a feature (Olympus Mons), but it does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify multiple major celestial objects, or discuss their general composition. It only provides a single fact about one feature of Mars, which is not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a volcano but does not explain what volcanoes are or how they are formed. It only states that Olympus Mons is a tall volcano on Mars, with no information about volcanic processes, formation, or structure. This is not direct support for the competency.

copy.en: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano in the solar system! It stands about 21 kilometres high — nearly three times taller than Mount Everest on Earth.
copy.tl: Ang Olympus Mons sa Mars ang pinakamatangkad na bulkan sa solar system! Humigit-kumulang 21 kilometro ang taas nito — halos tatlong beses na mas matangkad kaysa Mount Everest sa Earth.
copy.bis: Ang Olympus Mons sa Mars mao ang pinakataas nga bulkan sa solar system! Mga 21 kilometro ang gitas-on niini — hapit tulo ka beses nga mas taas kaysa sa Mount Everest sa Yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: commands from Earth take several minutes to reach a rover
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies radio signals travel through space but does not describe EMR as energy from vibrating charged particles or as transverse waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Since Mars is so far away
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: Mentions Mars and Earth but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their features, or composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: commands from Earth take several minutes to reach a rover
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: Radio communication is implied, but the card does not identify practical applications of EMR such as telecommunications, x-rays, or gamma rays.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: commands from Earth take several minutes to reach a rover
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves signals traveling from a source to a receiver but does not teach that waves carry energy.

copy.en: Since Mars is so far away, commands from Earth take several minutes to reach a rover. That means you can't drive it live like a video game!
copy.tl: Dahil napakalayo ng Mars, umaabot ng ilang minuto ang utos mula sa Earth bago marating ang rover—kaya hindi ito puwedeng i-drive nang live na parang video game!
copy.bis: Tungod kay layo kaayo ang Mars, ang sugo gikan sa Earth mokabat ug pipila ka minuto una makaabot sa rover—dili kini madrayb nga live sama sa video game!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gravity on Mars is weaker than on Earth, so you weigh less and can jump super high!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses gravity but focuses on Mars, not Earth, and does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or describe its predictable effects on objects on Earth. It only compares gravity between planets, which is related vocabulary but not direct support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gravity on Mars is weaker than on Earth, so you weigh less and can jump super high!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the effect of gravity on jumping, but it is about Mars, not observing/describing effects of gravity on the motion of an object on Earth. The competency requires Earth-based observation and description; the card's Mars context is only related.

copy.en:
Can you jump higher on Mars?

Yes! Gravity on Mars is weaker than on Earth, so you weigh less and can jump super high!
copy.tl:
Mas mataas ba kang makakatalon sa Mars?

Oo! Mas mahina ang grabidad sa Mars kaysa Mundo, kaya mas magaan ka at mas mataas kang makakatalon!
copy.bis:
Mas taas ba ka makalukso sa Mars?

Oo! Mas huyang ang grabidad sa Mars kaysa Yuta, mao nga mas gaan ka ug mas taas ka makalukso!
